selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline: node2 HTTP service healthy on private link before any changes
selected_evidence.summary: Showed node2 initially had no listener on 8080, then private IP 10.50.50.2 assigned, systemd HTTP service created/started and confirmed listening, firewalld opened, and node1 curl to 10.50.50.2:8080 returned the service content.

selected_evidence.requirement: Publish node2:8080 on node1's management address port 80, reachable by node3
selected_evidence.summary: opt1 interface configured, NAT rdr rule for lan:80(self)->10.50.50.2:8080 and hybrid outbound masquerade added; first test from node3 timed out (asymmetric routing), after masquerade fix node3's curl to http://10.100.215.10/ succeeded with HTTP 200 and node2's content.

selected_evidence.requirement: Same published port refused for every other source address
selected_evidence.summary: Explicit reject (block return) filter rule added ahead of default-allow, positioned after the node3-only pass rule; pfctl -s rules confirms ordering; node2 curl to node1:80 fails with 'Connection refused' both before and after the masquerade fix.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, boot-identity change, and recovery
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime=1788627138 with NAT/filter rules and interfaces confirmed healthy; reboot acknowledged then node unreachable; post-reboot kern.boottime=1788627515 (changed); NAT/filter rules and node3 connectivity (HTTP 200) confirmed recovered.

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, boot-identity change, and recovery
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id=deef5424... with service active/listening; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id=defa9202... (changed); service active, IP/firewalld zone restored, and node3 end-to-end request returned HTTP 200 afterward.

selected_evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, boot-identity change, and recovery
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id=4d340bf4... with working request to node1:80 (HTTP 200); reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id=c9e8a47f... (changed); node3's access to the published service confirmed still working (HTTP 200) and node2's refusal still enforced (curl exit 7) after all three restarts.

commands.command:
cat > /tmp/add_fwd.py <<'PYEOF'
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET, shutil
path = '/conf/config.xml'
shutil.copy(path, path + '.bak2')
tree = ET.parse(path)
root = tree.getroot()

# 1. disable anti-lockout so port 80 rdr to self isn't silently blocked
system = root.find('system')
webgui = system.find('webgui')
noal = webgui.find('noantilockout')
if noal is None:
    noal = ET.SubElement(webgui, 'noantilockout')
noal.text = '1'

# 2. NAT port-forward rule: lan:80 (self) -> 10.50.50.2:8080, source restricted to node3
nat = root.find('nat')
rule = ET.SubElement(nat, 'rule')
ET.SubElement(rule, 'interface').text = 'lan'
ET.SubElement(rule, 'ipprotocol').text = 'inet'
ET.SubElement(rule, 'protocol').text = 'tcp'
src = ET.SubElement(rule, 'source')
ET.SubElement(src, 'address').text = '10.100.215.12'
dst = ET.SubElement(rule, 'destination')
ET.SubElement(dst, 'network').text = 'lanip'
ET.SubElement(dst, 'port').text = '80'
ET.SubElement(rule, 'target').text = '10.50.50.2'
ET.SubElement(rule, 'local-port').text = '8080'
ET.SubElement(rule, 'descr').text = 'antrieb: forward lan:80 (node3 only) -> node2:8080'
ET.SubElement(rule, 'associated-rule-id').text = ''

tree.write(path, xml_declaration=True, encoding='utf-8')
print('nat rule + noantilockout added')
PYEOF
python3 /tmp/add_fwd.py
commands.stdout: nat rule + noantilockout added
